title: Special Leadership and Capacity-Building Programmes by Ministry of Minority Affairs for minority women in Odisha
body_text:
Under the erstwhile schemes of the Ministry of Minority Affairs, the Ministry implemented the Leadership Development of Minority Women (Nai Roshni) scheme to empower and build their confidence among minority women by providing knowledge, tools and techniques for interacting with Government systems, banks and other institutions at all levels. The scheme aimed to enhance leadership qualities, promote awareness about rights and entitlements, and facilitate socio-economic empowerment of minority women. The scheme was implemented across the country, including the State of Odisha, through empanelled Project Implementing Agencies.
Further, the Ministry has now subsumed various welfare schemes under the integrated umbrella scheme PM VIKAS (Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan). PM VIKAS focuses on the socio-economic and educational empowerment of six notified minority communities through skill development, Leadership & entrepreneurship development, education support and infrastructure-related interventions.
Minority women, including from the state of Odisha, are eligible to participate in and benefit from the various components of PM VIKAS, including skill development, Leadership Development & Entrepreneurship and related capacity-building initiatives, subject to the scheme guidelines.
This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Minority Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that its earlier Nai Roshni scheme, which built leadership skills among minority women including in Odisha, has now been subsumed into the integrated umbrella scheme PM VIKAS (Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan). Minority women in Odisha remain eligible for skill development, leadership and entrepreneurship, education support, and infrastructure interventions under PM VIKAS, subject to scheme guidelines. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju gave this information in a written reply.
enrichment.context:
Nai Roshni was launched in 2012-13 to empower minority women by enhancing their leadership qualities and awareness of rights, enabling better interaction with government systems, banks, and other institutions. Over time, the government has moved towards consolidating multiple minority welfare schemes into a single umbrella framework to reduce fragmentation, improve monitoring, and ensure convergence of resources. PM VIKAS, notified by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, merges several earlier schemes (including those related to skill development, education, and infrastructure) targeting the six notified minority communities—Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains.

This reflects a broader trend in governance of rationalizing centrally sponsored schemes into comprehensive umbrella programmes (similar to consolidations seen in other ministries) to achieve better outcomes and administrative efficiency. For UPSC aspirants, this development is relevant to understanding minority welfare architecture, women's empowerment initiatives, and the evolution of scheme design in Indian social policy.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Nai Roshni' scheme, mentioned in the context of minority women's empowerment, has been subsumed under which umbrella scheme?
options: PM VIKAS (Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that Nai Roshni and other welfare schemes of the Ministry of Minority Affairs have been subsumed under the integrated umbrella scheme PM VIKAS.

prelims_questions.question: PM VIKAS, implemented by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, targets how many notified minority communities?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies that PM VIKAS focuses on the socio-economic and educational empowerment of six notified minority communities.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the rationale behind consolidating multiple welfare schemes into umbrella programmes like PM VIKAS. Examine its implications for the effectiveness of minority welfare delivery in India.

Leadership development programmes for minority women aim at socio-economic empowerment through institutional engagement. Critically analyze the significance of such capacity-building initiatives in achieving gender and social justice goals in India.
